/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
import sys, importlib.util
print(sys.executable)
for name in ['pypdf','pdfplumber','fitz','pypdfium2','PIL']:
    spec=importlib.util.find_spec(name)
    print(name, spec.origin if spec else 'unavailable')
PY"

/bin/bash -c "mkdir -p tmp/pdfs && python3 - <<'PY'
from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
r=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
print('Pages:',len(r.pages))
print('Metadata:',r.metadata)
parts=[]
for i,p in enumerate(r.pages):
    parts.append(f'\\n\\n======== PAGE {i+1} ========\\n'+p.extract_text(extraction_mode='layout'))
Path('tmp/pdfs/manuscript.txt').write_text(''.join(parts))
print(''.join(parts)[:32000])
PY"

/bin/bash -c "ls -la /fsx/homes/Yaochen.Wang@mbzuai.ac.ae/AI-reviewer/utility/.runtime/ghostscript-9.55.0 && python3 - <<'PY'
from shutil import which
for name in ['gs','pdftoppm','pdftocairo','mutool','convert']:
    print(name,which(name))
PY"

/bin/bash -c "sed -n '540,700p' tmp/pdfs/manuscript.txt && python3 - <<'PY'
from pypdf import PdfReader
r=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
for p in [2,3,9]:
    print('\\n=== Plain text page',p+1,'===')
    print(r.pages[p].extract_text())
PY"

strengths: The paper addresses an important deployment problem: estimating performance when production labels are unavailable. Combining density-ratio estimation with weighted calibration is a practical approach with a sound population-level rationale under covariate shift and support overlap.

The evaluation is substantial within the tabular setting: 959 model–dataset cases and 36,557 production chunks. PAPE achieves the lowest reported errors across all six metric–evaluation combinations. Comparisons with IW using the same density-ratio estimator and with unweighted CBPE are particularly informative.

Normalizing estimation errors by reference sampling variability offers a useful operational perspective. Analyses across performance-change magnitudes and chunk sizes provide additional evidence beyond aggregate averages.
Public Folktables data, explicit temporal splits, a linked code repository, and hardware/runtime disclosure provide useful foundations for reproducibility.

The limitations section appropriately acknowledges concept shift, insufficient support overlap, calibration error, and sampling uncertainty. These acknowledgments strengthen the presentation. No material research-ethics concern is evident from the reported study.
weaknesses: The main technical gap concerns metric coverage. Equations (1)–(2) establish an identity for expectations of per-observation functions, such as accuracy and confusion-matrix entries. They do not directly cover F1, a nonlinear ratio, or AUROC, a pairwise ranking functional. The manuscript supplies neither metric-specific estimators nor corresponding derivations, leaving two of its three experimental metrics unsupported by the displayed algorithm. The claim of applicability to any performance metric is therefore too broad.

Equation (4) incorrectly equates expected absolute label residual with absolute conditional calibration error. For a perfectly calibrated Bernoulli(0.5) prediction, these quantities are 0.5 and 0, respectively. The intended calibration-error bound is repairable, but the distinction matters. Furthermore, the population argument assumes target calibration; it provides no error guarantee for the actual procedure using estimated density ratios and a fitted calibrator.

Essential implementation choices are missing from the manuscript: the density-ratio classifier and calibrator families, their objectives and hyperparameters, preprocessing, and random seeds. Algorithm 1 also evaluates the density-ratio classifier on its training reference observations without specifying overfitting controls. These details materially affect the method, so the repository link should be accompanied by a sufficiently complete experimental specification.

All experiments use temporal shifts within one census-data source. They do not establish that the shifts preserve P(Y|X), as required by the theory. Controlled covariate-shift experiments with known weights, together with target-calibration diagnostics, would help determine when and why the proposed adaptation succeeds. The sample-size analysis covers only one selected case.

The statistical evidence needs clearer treatment of dependence. The pairing unit for the Wilcoxon test is unspecified, and many chunks share datasets, reference samples, and monitored models. Reporting p = 0.0 does not resolve this issue. Cluster-aware confidence intervals, per-case effect distributions, and unscaled errors would make the practical and statistical significance of the aggregate improvements assessable.

Some benchmark adaptations are insufficiently justified. ATC and DoC were developed for accuracy, but their extensions to F1 and AUROC are not validated here. The random-resampling procedure used to train DoC also lacks a precise shift-generation specification. The IW and CBPE comparisons remain meaningful, but broader claims of superiority need stronger support.

Originality is primarily in integrating established density-ratio estimation and weighted calibration. The paper should more clearly distinguish its contribution from the cited adaptability/weighted-calibration work and explain the conditions under which it improves on direct IW. Clarity also needs attention: the abstract implies predictions alone suffice although Algorithm 1 requires input features, and Figures 1–2 label the proposed method 'M-CBPE' rather than PAPE.
